lessons.title: Choosing Handles, Locks, and Hinges for Local Conditions
lessons.body: In Africa, hardware must survive heat, dust, humidity, and salt air in coastal areas. Choose handles made from stainless steel 304 or powder-coated aluminum. Avoid cheap zinc alloy that rusts in months. For inland dry areas, nylon or UV-stabilized plastic handles can work but check they don't become brittle. Locks: use brass or stainless steel cylinders with at least 5 pins. In dusty regions, avoid exposed springs; choose enclosed mechanisms. Hinges: stainless steel 304 or 316 for coastal, with nylon washers to reduce friction. For heavy doors, use 3 hinges per door leaf, each rated for 40 kg. In hot climates, expansion gaps matter; choose hinges with adjustable height. Always test a sample: spray with salt water for 48 hours (coastal) or leave in sun for a week (inland). Local hardware shops often sell Chinese imports; ask for grade 304 stamp. For security, use multipoint locks with 3 locking points. In high-crime areas, add a secondary deadbolt. Budget: a good handle set costs $15-30, a lock cylinder $10-20, hinges $5-10 each. Don't mix metals that cause galvanic corrosion (e.g., aluminum and steel without barrier). Use nylon or Teflon tape between dissimilar metals. For sliding doors, choose rollers with sealed bearings and UV-resistant nylon wheels. In sandy areas, choose larger wheels (30mm) that ride over grit. Always keep spare parts; hardware fails first. Train yourself to identify quality: weight, smooth operation, no sharp edges, and a warranty of at least 2 years. Remember, cheap hardware costs more in replacements and customer complaints.

lessons.title: Installing Window Handles and Fasteners
lessons.body: Start by checking the window frame profile. Most aluminum windows have a Euro-groove or a specific channel. Measure the distance between the two mounting holes on your handle (common: 43mm or 55mm). If it doesn't match, you'll need an adapter plate or a different handle. Use a 3.5mm or 4mm drill bit for pilot holes in aluminum; never use wood bits. Drill at slow speed (800-1200 rpm) and use a few drops of kerosene or WD-40 as lubricant to prevent chips. For fasteners, use stainless steel self-tapping screws with a pan head. Length should be 10-12mm longer than the handle base thickness. For PVC or thermal break frames, use screws with a drill point. Insert screws by hand first to avoid cross-threading. Tighten firmly but not so tight that you crush the frame. For casement windows, the handle operates a multi-point lock; ensure the espagnolette bar moves freely. If stiff, adjust the striker plate on the frame. For sliding windows, handles are often surface-mounted with two screws; use a template to align. After installation, test open/close 10 times. If the handle feels loose, add a drop of threadlocker (blue) on screws. In dusty areas, apply silicone spray to the moving parts monthly. For security, choose handles with a key lock or a child safety catch. In coastal areas, apply a thin coat of petroleum jelly on screws to prevent rust. Common mistake: over-tightening screws, which strips the aluminum threads. If threads strip, use a larger screw or a rivet nut. Always wear safety glasses when drilling. Keep a vacuum or brush to clean aluminum shavings; they stain and cause corrosion. For a typical window, installation takes 15-20 minutes. Charge accordingly.

lessons.title: Installing Door Locks and Cylinders
lessons.body: Door locks for aluminum doors are usually mortise locks or narrow stile locks. First, determine the backset: the distance from the door edge to the center of the lock cylinder hole. Common backsets are 30mm, 35mm, and 40mm. Measure your door stile width; it must be at least 45mm for a standard mortise lock. Use a lock template or measure carefully. Drill the cylinder hole (usually 20mm) and the mortise pocket with a chisel or router. For narrow stile doors, use a lock with a 20mm faceplate. Cylinders: choose a euro profile cylinder with a length that matches door thickness plus 10mm. For example, a 45mm door needs a 55mm cylinder (45+10). If the cylinder sticks out, it's a security risk; use a security escutcheon. Install the cylinder from the outside, then the lock body from the inside. Secure with the long screw through the lock body into the cylinder. Test the key: it should turn smoothly without forcing. For double doors, use a flush bolt on the inactive leaf. In dusty areas, use a cylinder with a dust cover. For high security, choose a cylinder with drill resistance and at least 6 pins. Master keying is possible but keep it simple. After installation, adjust the strike plate so the latch enters freely. If the door sags, fix the hinges first. Lubricate the lock with graphite powder, not oil, which attracts dust. In coastal areas, use stainless steel or brass locks; avoid zinc. For emergency exit doors, use panic bars. Always keep a spare key outside the building. Cost: a good mortise lock set $25-50, cylinder $15-30. Installation time: 1-2 hours per door. Practice on a scrap door first.

lessons.title: Fitting Rollers and Tracks for Sliding Systems
lessons.body: Sliding aluminum doors and windows need smooth rollers and clean tracks. First, inspect the track: it should be straight, level, and free of debris. Use a vacuum and a wire brush to clean. For new installations, choose tracks with a raised centre rib to guide rollers. Rollers come in single, double, or tandem wheels. For heavy doors (over 40 kg), use tandem rollers with sealed bearings. Wheel diameter: 20-30mm for normal, 30-40mm for sandy areas. Material: nylon or polyurethane; avoid cheap plastic that flattens. Adjustable rollers are best; they have a screw to raise or lower the door by up to 5mm. Install rollers at the bottom of the door stile. Usually, there is a slot; slide the roller in and secure with a screw. For top-hung systems, rollers go on top. Ensure the roller is centered in the track. The door should slide with one finger. If it binds, check for debris, bent track, or misaligned rollers. For tracks, use stainless steel or anodized aluminum. In coastal areas, stainless steel 304 is best. Fix track with countersunk screws every 300mm. Use a spirit level to ensure it's flat. For sliding windows, the track often has a drainage hole; keep it clear. Lubricate tracks with silicone spray, never oil. For security, add anti-lift blocks to prevent the door being lifted out. In dusty regions, use brush seals on the track to keep out grit. Replace rollers when they develop flat spots or become noisy. A set of 4 rollers costs $10-20. Installation time: 30-60 minutes per door. Test by sliding 20 times. If the door jumps, adjust roller height. Always keep spare rollers.

lessons.title: Weather Stripping and Insect Screens
lessons.body: Weather stripping stops drafts, water, and dust. For aluminum windows and doors, use EPDM or silicone rubber seals. Avoid cheap foam that crumbles in heat. Common types: brush seals for sliding tracks, bulb seals for casement windows, and fin seals for doors. Measure the gap: for sliding windows, use a 5-7mm brush seal; for doors, a 10-12mm bulb seal. Clean the surface with alcohol before applying. Most seals have a self-adhesive backing; press firmly for 30 seconds. For better hold, use a small amount of superglue at the ends. In hot climates, choose UV-resistant silicone. Replace seals every 3-5 years. Insect screens: use aluminum or fiberglass mesh. Aluminum mesh is stronger but dents; fiberglass is cheaper but tears. For coastal areas, use stainless steel mesh to resist salt. Frame the mesh with aluminum U-channel and spline (rubber cord). Cut mesh 20mm larger than frame. Roll the spline into the groove with a screen roller tool. For windows, make screens removable for cleaning. For doors, use a hinged screen door with a closer. In areas with mosquitoes, use 18x16 mesh (18 holes per inch). For sandflies, use 20x20. Install screens on the outside of the frame. Keep screens tight; loose mesh lets insects in. Clean with a soft brush and soapy water. Repair small holes with clear nail polish or a patch kit. Cost: weather strip $1-2 per meter, screen mesh $5-10 per square meter. Installation time: 15-30 minutes per window. Always test for gaps with a light or smoke test.

lessons.title: Maintaining and Replacing Hardware
lessons.body: Hardware fails first. Set a maintenance schedule: every 3 months in dusty or coastal areas, every 6 months inland. Start by cleaning: use a soft cloth and mild soapy water. Never use abrasive cleaners or steel wool on aluminum. For locks, apply graphite powder or PTFE spray. For hinges, apply a drop of light machine oil (SAE 20) and wipe excess. For rollers, clean tracks and spray silicone. Check screws: tighten any loose ones. Look for rust: if you see white rust on aluminum, clean with a 50/50 vinegar water solution and apply a protective wax. For coastal areas, apply a corrosion inhibitor like Boeshield T-9 every 6 months. Replace hardware when: handles wobble, keys stick, rollers flatten, seals harden, or hinges squeak after lubrication. Keep a stock of common spares: handles, rollers, lock cylinders, and screws. When replacing, take the old part to the shop to match. For locks, if the key is lost, you can rekey a cylinder by replacing the pins, but it's easier to buy a new cylinder. For sliding doors, if the roller is not adjustable, replace with an adjustable type. In an emergency, you can use a screwdriver to pry a sliding door back onto track, but fix properly. Train customers: show them how to clean tracks and lubricate. Offer a 6-month service contract. Cost of maintenance: minimal, but saves expensive repairs. A well-maintained door lasts 20 years; neglected, 5. Always use the right tool: Allen keys, Phillips screwdrivers, and a small brush. Document what you did and when. This builds trust and repeat business.

quiz.q: Which material is best for handles in coastal Africa?
quiz.explanation: Stainless steel 304 resists salt corrosion better than other common materials.

quiz.q: What is the recommended number of hinges for a heavy door?
quiz.explanation: Three hinges distribute the weight of a heavy door and prevent sagging.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid mixing aluminum and steel without a barrier?
quiz.explanation: Dissimilar metals in contact can cause galvanic corrosion, especially in humid conditions.

quiz.q: What drill bit is used for pilot holes in aluminum?
quiz.explanation: A high-speed steel bit at slow speed with lubricant prevents damage to aluminum.

quiz.q: What is the common distance between mounting holes on a window handle?
quiz.explanation: 43mm is a standard spacing for many Euro-groove handles.

quiz.q: What should you use to lubricate a lock cylinder?
quiz.explanation: Graphite powder lubricates without attracting dust, unlike oil.

quiz.q: What is the backset of a door lock?
options: B) Distance from door edge to cylinder center
quiz.explanation: Backset is measured from the door edge to the center of the cylinder hole.

quiz.q: For a 45mm thick door, what cylinder length is recommended?
quiz.explanation: Cylinder length should be door thickness plus 10mm for proper fit.

quiz.q: What type of roller is best for sandy areas?
options: B) Large nylon with sealed bearings
quiz.explanation: Large nylon rollers with sealed bearings ride over grit and resist wear.

quiz.q: How often should you clean sliding tracks in dusty areas?
quiz.explanation: Dust builds up quickly and can damage rollers, so quarterly cleaning is needed.

quiz.q: What is the best material for weather stripping in hot climates?
quiz.explanation: EPDM and silicone resist UV and heat, unlike foam which crumbles.

quiz.q: What mesh size is recommended for mosquito protection?
quiz.explanation: 18x16 mesh is fine enough to keep out mosquitoes while allowing airflow.

quiz.q: How do you secure a spline in a screen frame?
options: B) Roll into groove with screen roller
quiz.explanation: A screen roller tool presses the spline into the groove, holding the mesh tight.

quiz.q: What should you do if a screw strips the aluminum threads?
quiz.explanation: A rivet nut provides new threads and a strong hold in stripped aluminum.

quiz.q: What is a sign that a roller needs replacing?
quiz.explanation: Flat spots or noise indicate worn rollers that no longer roll smoothly.

quiz.q: How often should you lubricate hinges in coastal areas?
quiz.explanation: Coastal salt air accelerates corrosion, so quarterly lubrication is needed.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of an anti-lift block on a sliding door?
options: A) To make it slide faster
B) To prevent the door being lifted out
quiz.explanation: Anti-lift blocks secure the door in the track, preventing forced removal.

quiz.q: What is the best way to clean aluminum hardware?
quiz.explanation: Mild soapy water cleans without scratching or damaging the protective coating.

quiz.q: What is white rust on aluminum?
quiz.explanation: White rust is aluminum oxide, which can be cleaned with vinegar and protected with wax.

quiz.q: What should you keep in stock for maintenance?
options: B) Common spares like rollers and screws
quiz.explanation: Having common spares on hand reduces downtime and improves service.

quiz.q: What is the recommended torque when tightening screws on aluminum?
quiz.explanation: Over-tightening can strip threads or deform the frame; firm is enough.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a striker plate?
quiz.explanation: The striker plate is mounted on the frame and receives the latch bolt.

quiz.q: What type of screw is best for aluminum window frames?
quiz.explanation: Stainless steel self-tapping screws resist corrosion and cut into aluminum.

quiz.q: How do you test weather stripping for gaps?
quiz.explanation: A light or smoke test reveals air leaks that indicate gaps in the seal.

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of pins for a secure lock cylinder?
quiz.explanation: Five pins provide a good level of security against picking.

quiz.q: What should you do before installing a handle?
quiz.explanation: Measuring ensures the handle matches the existing holes or template.

quiz.q: What is the best lubricant for sliding tracks?
quiz.explanation: Silicone spray lubricates without attracting dust or dirt.

quiz.q: How often should you replace weather stripping?
quiz.explanation: Weather stripping degrades over time, especially in harsh climates.

quiz.q: What is the advantage of adjustable rollers?
options: B) Can raise or lower door
quiz.explanation: Adjustable rollers allow you to align the door in the track for smooth operation.

quiz.q: What should you do if a key sticks in a lock?
quiz.explanation: Graphite powder lubricates the pins without gumming up the lock.
